strengths: Every road that changes the pools has one writer: adjust, set, fill, zero, grant, revoke and label each ask the primary when another GM is connected, and each asks again inside its serialWrite step so a GM that became the primary meanwhile takes it (scripts/despair.mjs:293-300, 330-350, 376-421, 449-507).

The owed Despair (E05 C12) is one pure arithmetic (`owedAfter`, `settlementOf`) with thin writers around it; every spending road reads the spendable pool after waiting for the other GMs' rows (scripts/despair.mjs:561-579, 721-736, 816-819, 916-917).

Despair to Hope has one road for both doors (`creditHopeFromDespair`): refused under the darkening, read from the Hope the GMs hold, capped by the Monocub's purse, the debt recorded before the Hope so no redrawn window offers it twice, and one veiled card (scripts/despair.mjs:861-891).

The roll's Despair award refuses reactions, unwitnessed rolls, forged GM flags, non-characters, Monokumas and plain 2d12 rolls, each with the measurement that put it there (scripts/despair-award.mjs:26-108, 284-290).
The critical rule corrects Daggerheart's funnel against a snapshot instead of replacing it, so a build that stops paying leaves it doing nothing (scripts/critical.mjs:55-107).
The price chain re-quotes at the moment of paying and hands back a receipt that knows a Burst from an action; a refund says only what landed (scripts/price.mjs:202-308).

Level Up: a player's picks are a claim judged on the primary against a named offer; an apply is one write and one step of `advances`; a take-back holds the latch until its drop; the Reinforced waits for the class's next verdict (scripts/level-up.mjs:418-448, 642-656, 812-1011, 1048-1122).

Trait rulings: the listed traits are read from this browser's config on both sides, never carried; the proposal is a claim dropped when off the list; a pass after 'Change to' voids the card's ruling (scripts/trait-ruling.mjs:136-141, 261-265, 321-350).

The safeword's caller is named only on a recipient-addressed socket to the GMs; the primary posts the public card; when no GM answers in time the caller's own browser posts it, header hidden; one pause, on the primary (scripts/safeword.mjs:277-363, 447-476).
Monocub moves are paid on the GM after every condition, one serial step per Monocub and one per target for the share and the price, so a refusal costs nothing (scripts/monocub.mjs:1270-1322).
A Rest's benefits and its 'used up' stamp are one write, and the window enforces the pick count live with the check after it kept as the authority (scripts/rest.mjs:353-361, 382-473).
resources.mjs keeps Daggerheart 2.12's optional-resource clean-up from deleting Actions by taking the one deletion out of the update, not by wrapping the system (scripts/resources.mjs:64-111).

findings.title: A GM that is not the primary counts a Despair Call as paid before the primary writes the pool, and the primary takes the price with no check
findings.what_happens: On a GM that is not the primary, spendDespairCall checks the spendable pool on this browser's copy, then adjustDespair(userId, -cost) goes to routeToPrimary, which sends `despair.adjust` with `void` and answers the pool it expects at once; spendDespairCall reads that as paid and the caller applies the Call. On the primary, handleDespair runs adjustDespair(delta) and writePool clamps at 0 - there is no price check there. So a pool the primary has lowered in the same round trip (another Call, a roll's point given back by a Reroll) pays less than the price, and an ask that is not answered (time-out, the primary's module not listening yet) leaves the Call applied and the pool untouched, while the bridge tells the GM the change was not carried out.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs: the Assistant GM with a granted pool reads 3 on its bar a moment after the primary paid 1 from that pool, buys a 3-Despair Call, the Call lands and the pool ends at 0 - a 3-Despair Call for 2; with the primary reloading, the same press applies the Call and the pool stays at 3.
findings.expected: The Call applied only on the primary's answer that the price was taken (the expected pool not read as paid), or the price checked on the primary.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for an await on the ask (none: `void`), for a price check in handleDespair or guardDespairDelta (the guard checks only |delta| <= 12 and non-zero), and for spendDespairCallFor checking the answer (it checks `ok` only, calls.mjs:470-475). The timing of the two writes is not read; tier 2 E37-T8 drives the set/fill/roster asks, not a Call bought on a second GM. The earlier reader of old-1.2.42-despair.json wrote this as suspected; the road is now traced end to end.
findings.old_id: DESP-LC1 (the live check of DESP-12, open; DESP-12's routing is what leaves this road)

findings.title: A Bounty that lapses on a GM that is not the primary can be told 'cancelled' while the primary's settlement has already paid its Despair
findings.where: scripts/despair.mjs:651-662 (returnOwed), 49-51 and 755-774 (settleOwed on the primary); scripts/monocub.mjs:1857-1881 (lapseBounties); scripts/clock.mjs:782-822 (applyTimeOfDayChange runs on the client that moved the clock)
findings.what_happens: lapseBounties runs on whichever GM moved the clock. returnOwed reads this GM's copy of `despairOwed` in a step of this browser's DESPAIR_KEY queue; its note says that queue orders it against the settlement 'on the primary', which is true only on the primary. The settlement runs on the primary on `drpgTimeOfDayChanged`. When the clock is moved by another GM, the row can still stand in that GM's copy after the primary has paid it; returnOwed then drops the tombstoned row and answers 'cancelled', nothing is given back, and the GMs' card says the owed Despair was cancelled. The pool has paid for a Bounty that lapsed - the double charge A113-C6-3 was written to stop.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs; the Assistant GM moves the clock to the afternoon with a Bounty open; the primary settles first, the pool drops by 1; on the Assistant's browser the row is still there, the card says 'its owed Despair is cancelled', and the pool keeps the drop.
findings.expected: The lapse's give-back asked of the primary (as every other pool change is), or decided against the settlement's mark rather than this browser's copy.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that lapseBounties is not gated to the primary (it asks only isGM, 1858) and that applyTimeOfDayChange runs on one client, the mover (clock.mjs comment 823-829). The order of the primary's settlement against the other GM's lapse depends on sync.mjs's merge window and the store's exchange, which I did not time; that is why this is suspected. On the primary the same road is ordered by DESPAIR_KEY and is right.

findings.title: On the GM's own Level Up picker a new experience left without a name is skipped and the rest written; in a verdict's batch that counts as given and drops the Blackened's waiting Reinforced

findings.what_happens: openAdvancement refuses a blank new experience on the player's road (648-651: nothing sent, the offer kept). On a GM's road it goes to applyAdvancement, which warns 'A new experience needs a name. That choice was skipped.' and writes the other picks and one step of `advances`. In runAdvancementBatch a GM pick that answers a summary is `applied`, and the row's waiting Reinforced is dropped from `deferredOfferStore`. findings.title: The Despair bar's + stepper is not held at the maximum: on a bar drawn before another change landed it spills into the overflow
findings.where: scripts/despair.mjs:1300-1305 (stepper +: adjustDespair(user.id, +1) with no clamp), 1256-1261 (the pip, clamped), 353-367 (an unclamped +1 over the maximum spills)
findings.what_happens: E17 fix e1-G4 made a pip's change `clamp: true` because a GM's correction that ran past the maximum spilled into the overflow and advanced a darkening. The + stepper beside the pips still calls adjustDespair(user.id, +1) unclamped; its `disabled` is the drawn `held >= max`. A pool raised to 12 by the primary (a roll's point) before this bar redraws leaves the + live, and its +1 spills 1 into the overflow.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM sees a pool at 11 and presses + just as a student's roll with Despair fills it on the primary: the pool stays 12 and the overflow counter goes up by 1, a step toward a darkening nobody earned.
findings.expected: The stepper held at the maximum as the pip is (`clamp: true`), unless spilling by hand is meant; then said in the tooltip.
findings.refutation_tried: Tier 2 E17-T8 (tests-tier2.mjs:86834) drives the pip only; no test drives the stepper. The tooltip says 'Adds 1 Despair to this pool' (DRPG.Tips.Gm.plusTooltip), not that it may spill. The window is one round trip, so the severity is minor.

findings.title: The Monocub's Hope and a Bribe payer's Hope are read off the document on the GM, not as the GMs hold them
findings.what_happens: price.mjs, rest.mjs, despair.mjs (creditHopeFromDespair) and level-up.mjs read and write a student's Hope on a GM through sheet-audit.mjs `meansWrite`, because (E29 fix r2-H24) a console's raised value read off the document and written back by a GM becomes the student's new mark. The Monocub roads compute their checks and writes from `resourceValue(actor, "hope")` directly and write through trustedWrite as the GM. A console's raised Hope on the Monocub (or on a Bribe's payer) that the audit has not put back yet passes the price check and is written back, less the price, as a GM's value.
findings.failure_scenario: A Monocub's player writes Hope 6 from the console and at once asks for Confusion: the GM's check passes on 6, the GM writes 5, and the audit may take 5 as the GMs' value instead of putting the console's write back.
findings.expected: The Monocub's and the payer's Hope read and written in the student's audit queue (`meansWrite`), as the other price roads do.
findings.refutation_tried: Read resource-guard.mjs `noteOwnWrite` (327-347): a GM's own trustedWrite is told to sheet-audit.mjs `noteOwnDropped`, which may judge the leaves it drops; I did not read noteOwnDropped through, so whether the audit still puts the console's value back is not settled. R3808 holds only that the file does not read the sheet's Hope without the purse. Suspected: needs a probe (a console write and a move in one tick, on the harness).

findings.title: A roll granted after no GM was connected gives its Despair through a protection from Despair
findings.where: scripts/roll-draw.mjs:3028-3030 (grantRolls: awardRollDespair(actor, 1)); scripts/despair-award.mjs:121-128 (the shield is asked only with a message)
findings.what_happens: awardRollDespair takes a room action's protection from Despair (timed-effects.mjs `takeDespairShield`) only when it is handed the roll's message. The fresh roll's road hands it (despair-award.mjs:104); the GMs' Grant of a roll thrown with no GM connected calls awardRollDespair(actor, 1) with none, though `rows` carries the message (roll-draw.mjs:2998). So the shield is neither used nor consulted, and the Monokuma gets the point.
findings.failure_scenario: A student holding 'next roll with Fear gives no Despair' rolls with Fear while the GM is away; the GM comes back and presses Grant all: the pool gains 1 and the protection still stands for a later roll.
findings.expected: The Grant hands the message, so the shield takes the point (and marks the roll for its Reroll) as at a fresh roll.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked the config's rule ('The character's next roll with Fear gives its Monokuma no Despair', config.mjs:2270-2272) - it does not exclude a roll granted later; checked takeDespairShield needs the primary (it does; decideUnwitnessed's grant runs on a GM, which may not be the primary - then the shield is skipped either way). No test of a Grant with a shield found by name.

not_established.item: Finding 2's order: whether the primary's settlement can run before a second GM's lapse of a Bounty in one change of the time of day.

l1.what: A lapsed Bounty's Despair when the clock is moved by a GM that is not the primary.
recipe: Two GMs, both with pools; note pool P of the primary GM.
As the primary, post a Bounty (Despair Call) on a living student; the GM bar shows 1 owed.
As the second GM, advance the time of day.
Read P on both bars and the GMs' card about the lapse.
l1.settles_if: P back where it was and the card says cancelled or given back: no defect; P one lower with a 'cancelled' card: finding 2 stands.

not_established.item: Finding 1 at a table (DESP-LC1): two GMs, one buying Despair Calls from its own pool while the primary awards roll points; the bar against the sum of awards and prices over a session.

l1.what: Whether a Call bought on a second GM ever pays less than its price or none.
recipe: Two GMs; grant the Assistant GM a pool and set it to 3.
As the primary, lower that pool by 1 by hand (pip) and, within a second, as the Assistant buy a 3-Despair Call.
Repeat with the primary's browser reloading while the Assistant buys.
Read the pool and whether the Call was applied.
l1.clients: 2 GMs (one Assistant with a granted pool), 1 player
l1.settles_if: Every applied Call took its full price: refuted; a Call applied with the pool at 0 after holding 2, or applied with the pool unchanged: stands.

not_established.item: Finding 6: whether sheet-audit.mjs `noteOwnDropped` (reached through resource-guard.mjs noteOwnWrite) still puts back a console's raised Hope that a Monocub road read and wrote less its price.

l1.what: A Monocub's console-raised Hope spent by a move in the same tick.
recipe: A Monocub with 0 Hope; on its player's console write system.resources.hope.value = 6 and in the same tick call game.drpg for a Confusion (or press it).
Read the Monocub's Hope after the primary's audit, and game.drpg.sheetWrites().
l1.settles_if: Hope back to 0 and the move refused or flagged: refuted; Hope 5 standing: stands.

The record's `dice` shape (roll-draw.mjs keepRecord) was not traced.

l1.what: Not a table check: a harness probe that draws a roll with advantage and a Call's d4 with the balance log on and reads the row.

l1.settles_if: adv.faces matches the advantage die and the Call's die is in flat or listed: no defect; otherwise a nit in the report's numbers.

not_established.item: price.mjs: two payPrice calls on a player's browser begun before the first write lands (comment against code above) - whether a real table can press two priced controls inside one round trip.

l1.what: Two priced actions in one breath on one player's browser.

Read the Hope and Sanity after.
l1.settles_if: One paid with Hope and the other with Sanity (or refused): the comment holds; both paid with the one Hope: the comment is wrong at a table.
